activity_context.topic_title: Symmetry Properties of the Standard Normal Distribution

examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on a Bounded Interval
examples.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.53 <        Z <        0.53).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/bb86bde3595d6a64d1cd82da3c928f28c496f495f9c6815e56ee025a4a69d685.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$ 

$$
P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.53<Z<0.53) & =P(Z<0.53)-P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.53)-P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =Φ(0.53)-Φ(-0.53)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(0.53) = 0.7019,
$$

but we are not given $\Phi(-0.53) .$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.53) & =P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.53) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.53) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.53) \\  & =1-Φ(0.53) \\  & =1-0.7019 \\  & =0.2981\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.53<Z<0.53) & =Φ(0.53)-Φ(-0.53) \\  & =0.7019-0.2981 \\  & =0.4038.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<1.94).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.0\,$ | $\,0.0224\,$ | $\,0.0217\,$ | $\,0.0212\,$ |
| $\,-1.9\,$ | $\,0.0274\,$ | $\,0.0268\,$ | $\,0.0262\,$ |
| $\,-1.8\,$ | $\,0.0344\,$ | $\,0.0336\,$ | $\,0.0329\,$ |

$P(Z<1.94)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/0316b85ed769fd2688538ed2c9a47236db0890bf52bf7fcbad021f7d509373b4.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<1.94).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/e708b9dc6927a17f193c216f1b14b1b9ef98e6d9d26a998790112863661ca5d0.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>-1.94).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/43f1e2eb5354cbdcd5ff359985048fa2d6411167ad5f50fe45c730642e184b61.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<1.94) & =P(Z>-1.94) \\  & =1-P(Z<-1.94) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.94) \\  & =1-0.0262 \\  & =0.9738.\end{aligned}
$$
